metadata.title: CareQuest Health Awareness Quiz Bank
metadata.description: Public-health education quiz content for RAG-based patient engagement. Each question is sourced from WHO or equivalent authoritative fact sheets. Use category 'patient_niche' to match questions to a patient's condition profile.
usage_notes: These are general public-health education questions, not personalized medical advice.
A clinician should approve which categories are shown to which patient profiles.
Numeric statistics reflect each source's publication/review date and may be updated periodically by WHO; verify before production use.
Recommended retrieval pattern: match patient_niche tags to a patient's condition(s), then retrieve a mixed set across 2-3 relevant categories rather than one category alone.

heart_cardiovascular.title: Heart & Cardiovascular Health
heart_cardiovascular.patient_niche: hypertension, heart disease, post-cardiac-event, stroke risk

questions.question: What is the leading cause of death globally?
questions.explanation: CVDs cause an estimated 19.8 million deaths per year, about 32% of all global deaths.

questions.question: What percentage of cardiovascular disease deaths are caused by heart attacks and strokes?
questions.explanation: Over 3 in 4 CVD deaths are due to heart attack and stroke.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a major behavioural risk factor for heart disease?
questions.explanation: The main behavioural risks are unhealthy diet, inactivity, tobacco, and harmful alcohol use.

questions.question: What is the leading risk factor driving cardiovascular disease in Europe?
questions.explanation: Hypertension caused almost a quarter of Europe's CVD deaths in 2019.

questions.question: How much moderate-intensity aerobic activity per week is recommended to help protect heart health?
questions.explanation: WHO recommends 150–300 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic activity weekly for adults.

questions.question: Which dietary change is recommended to reduce cardiovascular risk?
questions.explanation: WHO recommends reducing salt, eating more fruits/vegetables, and regular physical activity.

questions.question: Rheumatic heart disease is caused by complications of which untreated infection?
questions.explanation: Rheumatic heart disease results from damage caused by rheumatic fever, triggered by untreated strep throat.

questions.question: What is considered a healthy adult resting blood pressure range approximately?
questions.explanation: Normal blood pressure is generally around 120/80 mmHg; higher levels indicate hypertension risk.

questions.question: Which region reports the highest proportion of deaths from cardiovascular disease among WHO regions?
questions.explanation: CVDs account for 42.5% of all deaths in the WHO European Region, the highest proportion globally.

questions.question: What is the most effective way to detect cardiovascular disease early?
options: Only visiting a doctor during emergencies
questions.explanation: Early detection through screening allows management with counselling and medicines before serious events occur.

questions.question: Which everyday habit change is proven to reduce cardiovascular disease risk?
options: Reducing salt intake and eating more fruits and vegetables
questions.correct_answer: Reducing salt intake and eating more fruits and vegetables
questions.explanation: WHO confirms that reducing dietary salt and eating more fruit and vegetables reduces cardiovascular disease risk.

questions.question: What role does harmful alcohol use play in cardiovascular health?
options: It has no effect on the heart
It is one of the major behavioural risk factors for heart disease
It only affects the liver, not the heart
questions.correct_answer: It is one of the major behavioural risk factors for heart disease
questions.explanation: Harmful use of alcohol is listed among the most important behavioural risk factors for cardiovascular disease.

diabetes_metabolic.title: Diabetes & Metabolic Health
diabetes_metabolic.source: WHO Diabetes Fact Sheet, IDF Diabetes Prevention

questions.question: Type 2 diabetes occurs when the body cannot effectively use which hormone?
questions.explanation: Diabetes occurs when the pancreas doesn't produce enough insulin or the body can't use it effectively.

questions.question: How many minutes of moderate exercise per week helps prevent type 2 diabetes?
questions.explanation: WHO recommends at least 150 minutes of moderate exercise weekly to help prevent type 2 diabetes.

questions.question: What percentage of cardiovascular deaths were linked to high blood glucose according to WHO?
questions.explanation: Around 11% of cardiovascular deaths were caused by high blood glucose.

questions.question: Which of these habits helps delay or prevent type 2 diabetes onset?
questions.explanation: A healthy weight, physical activity, and a balanced diet help prevent type 2 diabetes.

questions.question: Which beverage choice is recommended over sugar-sweetened drinks for diabetes prevention?
questions.explanation: IDF recommends choosing water, coffee, or tea instead of sugar-sweetened beverages.

questions.question: How many servings of vegetables are recommended daily for diabetes prevention?
questions.explanation: IDF recommends eating at least three servings of vegetables daily, including leafy greens.

questions.question: Which type of fat should replace saturated fats to support metabolic health?
questions.explanation: Unsaturated fats like olive, canola, and sunflower oil are healthier alternatives to saturated fats.

questions.question: What is a key recommended regular test for people managing diabetes?
options: Blood glucose and glycated hemoglobin testing
questions.correct_answer: Blood glucose and glycated hemoglobin testing
questions.explanation: Regular blood glucose and HbA1c testing helps monitor and manage diabetes.

questions.question: Which grain choice supports better blood sugar management?
questions.explanation: Whole grains are recommended over refined/white grain products for metabolic health.

questions.question: Limiting alcohol intake to how many standard drinks per day is recommended for diabetes prevention?
questions.explanation: IDF recommends limiting alcohol to a maximum of two standard drinks per day.

questions.question: Which food choice is recommended over red or processed meat for better metabolic health?
options: Lean poultry, white meat, or seafood
questions.correct_answer: Lean poultry, white meat, or seafood
questions.explanation: IDF recommends choosing lean cuts of white meat, poultry, or seafood instead of red or processed meat.

liver_hepatitis.title: Liver Health & Hepatitis
liver_hepatitis.patient_niche: hepatitis A/B/C/D/E, liver disease, cirrhosis risk
liver_hepatitis.source: WHO Hepatitis Fact Sheets (A, B, C, D, E)

questions.question: How many main types of hepatitis viruses are there?
questions.explanation: There are 5 main hepatitis virus types: A, B, C, D, and E.

questions.question: Which hepatitis viruses have a safe and effective vaccine available?
questions.explanation: Safe, effective vaccines exist for hepatitis A and B; there is currently no vaccine for hepatitis C.

questions.question: How is hepatitis A primarily transmitted?
options: Through contaminated food and water (fecal-oral route)
questions.correct_answer: Through contaminated food and water (fecal-oral route)
questions.explanation: Hepatitis A spreads via fecal-oral contamination, linked to unsafe water and poor sanitation.

questions.question: When should the hepatitis B vaccine ideally be given to a newborn?
options: Only if the mother requests it
questions.explanation: The hepatitis B birth dose within 24 hours significantly reduces mother-to-child transmission risk.

questions.question: Approximately how many people worldwide live with chronic hepatitis B or C infection?
questions.explanation: WHO estimates 325 million people live with chronic hepatitis B or C infection worldwide.

questions.question: What is a key prevention method against hepatitis B and C transmission?
questions.explanation: Sterile injection equipment and screened blood transfusions prevent hepatitis B and C transmission.

questions.question: Hepatitis C is best prevented by avoiding contact with what?
questions.explanation: Since there's no hepatitis C vaccine, avoiding contact with infected blood is the primary prevention method.

questions.question: What long-term complications can chronic hepatitis B or C cause in the liver?
questions.explanation: Chronic hepatitis B/C infection can progress to cirrhosis and liver cancer if untreated.

questions.question: Hepatitis E is mainly transmitted through which route?
questions.explanation: Hepatitis E spreads primarily via the fecal-oral route, largely through contaminated water.

questions.question: Which practice helps prevent hepatitis D infection?
options: Hepatitis D has no relation to other hepatitis types
questions.explanation: Hepatitis D only infects people already infected with hepatitis B, so the HBV vaccine prevents it.

kidney_health.title: Kidney Health
kidney_health.patient_niche: chronic kidney disease, dialysis patients, diabetic nephropathy risk

questions.question: Which lifestyle factor helps reduce the risk of developing chronic kidney disease (CKD)?
options: Regular physical activity and healthy body weight
questions.correct_answer: Regular physical activity and healthy body weight
questions.explanation: A healthy lifestyle including physical activity, healthy weight, and no tobacco use reduces CKD risk.

questions.question: Which existing conditions increase the risk of chronic kidney disease if poorly controlled?
questions.explanation: Good control of blood pressure, glucose, and lipids in these conditions helps reduce CKD risk.

questions.question: What can help further reduce kidney disease risk in people with diabetes?
options: Good control of blood pressure, glucose, and lipids
questions.correct_answer: Good control of blood pressure, glucose, and lipids
questions.explanation: Controlling these three factors alongside lifestyle measures reduces CKD progression risk.

questions.question: Which of these habits does NOT help reduce chronic kidney disease risk?
questions.explanation: Refraining from tobacco use, not using it, is what helps reduce CKD risk.

questions.question: Why is blood pressure control especially important for kidney health?
options: It has no connection to kidney function
Uncontrolled high blood pressure can damage the kidneys over time
Blood pressure and kidneys are unrelated organs
questions.correct_answer: Uncontrolled high blood pressure can damage the kidneys over time
questions.explanation: Hypertension is a major risk factor for chronic kidney disease progression, so blood pressure control helps protect kidney function.

skin_uv_protection.title: Skin Health & Sun Protection
skin_uv_protection.patient_niche: skin cancer risk, dermatology patients, outdoor workers
skin_uv_protection.source: WHO Ultraviolet Radiation Fact Sheet, IARC European Code Against Cancer

questions.question: What is the primary cause of most skin cancers?
questions.explanation: Skin cancers are primarily caused by UV radiation from the sun or artificial sources like sunbeds.

questions.question: At what UV index level is sun protection recommended?
questions.explanation: WHO recommends sun protection when the UV index reaches 3 or higher.

questions.question: What percentage of skin cancer cases could be prevented with proper sun protection?
questions.explanation: Experts estimate 4 out of 5 skin cancer cases could be prevented through sun protection.

questions.question: What is the recommended minimum SPF for sunscreen during everyday activities?
questions.explanation: WHO/IARC recommend at least SPF 15 for daily activities and SPF 30+ during prolonged sun exposure.

questions.question: When are the sun's UV rays typically strongest during the day?
options: Two hours before to two hours after solar noon
questions.correct_answer: Two hours before to two hours after solar noon
questions.explanation: UV intensity peaks around midday, so limiting exposure during this window reduces risk.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT an effective sun protection measure?
options: Using artificial tanning beds for vitamin D
questions.correct_answer: Using artificial tanning beds for vitamin D
questions.explanation: Sunbeds increase skin cancer risk and should never be used as a vitamin D source.

questions.question: How often should sunscreen be reapplied during outdoor activity?
options: Every two hours, especially after sweating or swimming
questions.correct_answer: Every two hours, especially after sweating or swimming
questions.explanation: Sunscreen should be reapplied every two hours and after sweating, swimming, or towel-drying.

questions.question: Should sunscreen be used to extend time spent in the sun?
options: Yes, it makes sun exposure completely safe
No, it should not be used to justify longer sun exposure
It has no effect either way
questions.correct_answer: No, it should not be used to justify longer sun exposure
questions.explanation: WHO states sunscreens should not be used to extend sun exposure time, as they cannot completely block UV radiation.

questions.question: Which population is particularly vulnerable to sun damage requiring extra protection?
options: None, risk is equal for all ages
questions.explanation: Children are especially vulnerable to UV damage, which contributes to skin cancer risk later in life.

questions.question: Why are wraparound-style sunglasses recommended for sun protection?
options: They provide 99-100% UV-A and UV-B protection for the eyes
They are required by law everywhere
questions.correct_answer: They provide 99-100% UV-A and UV-B protection for the eyes
questions.explanation: WHO recommends wraparound sunglasses that block 99-100% of UV-A and UV-B rays to protect the eyes.

obesity_nutrition.title: Obesity, Weight & Nutrition
obesity_nutrition.patient_niche: overweight/obesity management, general wellness, weight-loss programs
obesity_nutrition.source: WHO Obesity and Healthy Diet Fact Sheets

questions.question: What BMI range does WHO consider healthy for adults?
questions.explanation: WHO recommends a BMI between 18.5 and 25 as a healthy range for adults.

questions.question: How many grams of fruits and vegetables does WHO recommend eating daily?
questions.explanation: WHO recommends at least 400g, or 5 portions, of fruits and vegetables daily.

questions.question: What percentage of daily energy intake should come from free sugars at most?
questions.explanation: WHO recommends limiting free sugar intake to under 10% of daily energy, ideally under 5%.

questions.question: What is the recommended daily salt intake limit according to WHO?
questions.explanation: WHO recommends limiting salt intake to less than 5 grams per day.

questions.question: Which type of fat should be limited to less than 1% of daily energy intake?
questions.explanation: WHO recommends limiting trans fat intake to less than 1% of total daily energy.

questions.question: How many people die each year globally due to being overweight or obese?
questions.explanation: Obesity and overweight contribute to at least 2.8 million deaths annually worldwide.

questions.question: What defines obesity in terms of BMI?
questions.explanation: A BMI over 25 is overweight; a BMI over 30 is classified as obese.

questions.question: Which food choice supports weight management?
questions.explanation: Increasing intake of nuts, whole grains, legumes, fruits, and vegetables supports healthy weight.

questions.question: How much daily physical activity is recommended for children to prevent obesity?
questions.explanation: WHO recommends 60 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity daily for children.

questions.question: Which infant feeding practice is recommended to help prevent childhood obesity?
options: Exclusive breastfeeding for the first 6 months
questions.correct_answer: Exclusive breastfeeding for the first 6 months
questions.explanation: Exclusive breastfeeding for 6 months, continued to 24 months, supports healthy weight development.

questions.question: How does regular physical activity combined with a healthy diet help with weight management?
options: It helps balance calories consumed and burned, supporting healthy weight
Diet and exercise work against each other
questions.correct_answer: It helps balance calories consumed and burned, supporting healthy weight
questions.explanation: WHO notes that regular physical activity together with a healthy diet is key to maintaining a healthy body weight.

questions.question: Which snack choice is a healthier alternative to sugary or fried snacks?
questions.explanation: IDF recommends nuts, fresh fruit, or unsweetened yoghurt as healthier snack alternatives.

mental_health.title: Mental Health & Wellbeing
mental_health.patient_niche: depression, anxiety, stress management, general mental wellness

questions.question: What percentage of the global burden of disease is made up by mental, neurological, and substance use disorders?
questions.explanation: These disorders make up 10% of the global burden of disease and 30% of non-fatal disease burden.

questions.question: How much does depression and anxiety cost the global economy in lost productivity each year?
questions.explanation: The global economy loses roughly US$1 trillion per year in productivity due to depression and anxiety.

questions.question: Approximately how many people worldwide were living with depression in 2023?
questions.explanation: WHO estimated 322 million people were living with depression in 2023, including 43 million children and adolescents.

questions.question: Which of these is a recognized category of mental disorder?
questions.explanation: Anxiety disorders, depression, bipolar disorder, and PTSD are among WHO-recognized mental disorders.

questions.question: Which factor contributes to the global burden of mental disorders?
questions.explanation: Depression and anxiety disorders are major contributors to the global disease burden and lost productivity.

questions.question: Approximately how many children and adolescents were living with depression in 2023?
questions.explanation: Of the 322 million people living with depression in 2023, 43 million were children and adolescents.

physical_activity_sports.title: Physical Activity & Sports
physical_activity_sports.patient_niche: sports medicine, rehabilitation, general fitness, chronic disease management
physical_activity_sports.source: WHO Guidelines on Physical Activity and Sedentary Behaviour

questions.question: How many minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic activity per week does WHO recommend for adults?
questions.explanation: WHO recommends 150–300 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic activity weekly for substantial health benefits.

questions.question: How many days per week should adults do muscle-strengthening activities?
questions.explanation: WHO recommends muscle-strengthening activities involving major muscle groups on 2 or more days weekly.

questions.question: What is the minimum duration recommended for a single bout of aerobic activity?
questions.explanation: Aerobic activity should ideally be performed in bouts of at least 10 minutes.

questions.question: Is physical activity still beneficial for people with chronic conditions or disabilities?
options: No, they should avoid all activity
Yes, with guidance suited to their condition
Only if they are fully cured first
Physical activity has no benefit for them
questions.correct_answer: Yes, with guidance suited to their condition
questions.explanation: WHO guidelines include specific recommendations for people with chronic conditions and disabilities, emphasizing that some activity is better than none.

questions.question: What is the WHO's key message about physical activity amounts?
options: Some physical activity is better than none
You must exercise for hours to benefit
Physical activity is optional for health
questions.correct_answer: Some physical activity is better than none
questions.explanation: WHO guidelines emphasize that all physical activity counts and any amount is better than none.

questions.question: How much moderate-to-vigorous physical activity is recommended daily for children and adolescents?
questions.explanation: WHO recommends an average of 60 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous activity daily for children and adolescents.

questions.question: Which behaviour should be limited across all age groups according to WHO physical activity guidance?
questions.explanation: WHO guidelines recommend limiting sedentary time across all age groups and abilities.

questions.question: For additional health benefits beyond the base recommendation, how many minutes of moderate activity can adults aim for weekly?
options: Physical activity has a fixed cap
questions.explanation: For extra benefits, adults may increase moderate-intensity activity beyond 300 minutes weekly, when appropriate.

questions.question: Why is muscle-strengthening activity important in addition to aerobic exercise?
options: It provides additional health benefits beyond aerobic activity alone
It replaces the need for aerobic activity entirely
It is only necessary for athletes
questions.correct_answer: It provides additional health benefits beyond aerobic activity alone
questions.explanation: WHO recommends muscle-strengthening activities on 2+ days weekly as they provide additional health benefits beyond aerobic exercise.

questions.question: How many organs does tobacco use damage in the body?
questions.explanation: Tobacco damages nearly every organ, causing cancer, heart disease, stroke, lung disease, and more.

questions.question: What chronic respiratory disease is tobacco smoking the leading cause of?
questions.explanation: Tobacco smoking is the leading cause of COPD, causing painful cough and breathing difficulties.

questions.question: Roughly how many chemicals does tobacco smoke contain, with at least 69 known to cause cancer?
questions.explanation: Tobacco smoke contains over 7,000 chemicals, at least 69 of which are known carcinogens.

questions.question: How many deaths globally are caused by second-hand smoke exposure each year?
questions.explanation: Over 1 million deaths globally each year are caused by exposure to second-hand smoke.

questions.question: What happens to respiratory health improvement after a person quits smoking?
questions.explanation: Quitting smoking leads to significant respiratory improvement and reduced hospitalization frequency.

questions.question: What percentage of lung cancer deaths globally are attributed to tobacco smoking?
questions.explanation: Tobacco smoking is responsible for over two-thirds of lung cancer deaths globally.

hydration_general_wellness.title: Hydration & General Wellness
hydration_general_wellness.patient_niche: general wellness, kidney patients, all-purpose daily habits

questions.question: Why is adequate hydration important for kidney health?
options: It has no relation to kidney function
It helps kidneys filter waste effectively
questions.correct_answer: It helps kidneys filter waste effectively
questions.explanation: Proper hydration supports healthy kidney function and waste filtration.

questions.question: Which drink choice is preferable for daily hydration over sugary beverages?
questions.explanation: Water is the healthiest primary choice for daily hydration, avoiding added sugars.

questions.question: What is a simple daily habit that supports overall wellness and hydration?
options: Choosing water over sugary drinks throughout the day
questions.correct_answer: Choosing water over sugary drinks throughout the day
questions.explanation: Prioritizing water over sugar-sweetened beverages supports hydration, dental health, and weight management.

eye_vision_health.title: Eye & Vision Health
eye_vision_health.patient_niche: diabetic retinopathy, cataract patients, elderly vision care
eye_vision_health.source: WHO Blindness and Visual Impairment Fact Sheet

questions.question: What are the two leading causes of vision impairment and blindness globally?
questions.explanation: Globally, uncorrected refractive errors and unoperated cataracts are the leading causes of vision impairment.

questions.question: Approximately how many people worldwide have a near or distance vision impairment?
questions.explanation: WHO estimates at least 2.2 billion people globally have vision impairment.

questions.question: What proportion of global vision impairment cases could have been prevented or is yet to be addressed?
questions.explanation: At least 1 billion of the 2.2 billion vision impairment cases could have been prevented or addressed.

questions.question: Which age group is most commonly affected by vision impairment and blindness?
questions.explanation: Most people with vision impairment and blindness are over the age of 50.

questions.question: Which systemic diseases can also contribute to eye conditions if poorly managed?
questions.explanation: Managing diabetes and hypertension effectively helps reduce the risk of related ocular diseases like diabetic retinopathy.

questions.question: What is recommended to detect and manage most eye conditions early?
questions.explanation: Early detection and timely management can prevent the majority of vision impairment and blindness cases.

oral_dental_health.title: Oral & Dental Health
oral_dental_health.patient_niche: dental patients, pediatric oral care, pregnancy oral health
oral_dental_health.source: WHO Oral Health Fact Sheet, WHO Sugars and Dental Caries

questions.question: How often should you brush your teeth with fluoride toothpaste according to WHO?
questions.explanation: WHO recommends twice-daily tooth brushing with fluoride toothpaste (1000-1500 ppm).

questions.question: What is the most common noncommunicable disease worldwide?
questions.explanation: Dental caries affects an estimated 2.5 billion people, making it the most common NCD globally.

questions.question: What dietary factor is the most common risk factor for dental caries?
questions.explanation: Consumption of free sugars in foods and drinks is the most common risk factor for dental caries.

questions.question: Should children under 2 years of age consume sugar-sweetened beverages?
options: No, WHO recommends avoiding them entirely
There is no guidance on this
questions.correct_answer: No, WHO recommends avoiding them entirely
questions.explanation: WHO recommends that children under 2 should not consume any sugar-sweetened beverages.

questions.question: Which practice helps prevent oral cancer and gum disease?
options: Stopping all forms of tobacco use
questions.correct_answer: Stopping all forms of tobacco use
questions.explanation: Stopping tobacco use, including chewing, significantly reduces oral cancer and gum disease risk.

questions.question: What is recommended to protect teeth during contact sports?
questions.explanation: Wearing protective gear like a mouth guard during contact sports reduces the risk of facial and dental injuries.

hand_hygiene_infection_prevention.title: Hand Hygiene & Infection Prevention
hand_hygiene_infection_prevention.patient_niche: post-surgical patients, hospital-acquired infection risk, general infection control

questions.question: What is described as the most important measure to prevent the spread of harmful germs in healthcare settings?
questions.explanation: Hand hygiene is the most important measure to avoid transmission of harmful germs and prevent healthcare-associated infections.

questions.question: When should you wash hands with soap and water instead of using alcohol-based hand rub?
options: When hands are visibly dirty or soiled
Never, alcohol rub is always better
questions.correct_answer: When hands are visibly dirty or soiled
questions.explanation: Soap and water should be used when hands are visibly dirty, soiled with body fluids, or after using the toilet.

questions.question: By how much can good infection prevention and control, including hand hygiene, reduce healthcare-associated infections?
questions.explanation: Effective infection prevention and control measures, including hand hygiene, can prevent up to 70% of healthcare-associated infections.

questions.question: How much can proper hand hygiene reduce diarrhoeal disease in community settings?
questions.explanation: WHO/UNICEF guidelines note that hand hygiene reduces diarrhoeal disease by about 30% in community settings.

questions.question: Which of these is one of the five key times WHO recommends practicing hand hygiene?
options: Once a day regardless of activity
questions.explanation: Key times include before preparing food, before eating, after using the toilet, and after coughing or sneezing.

cancer_prevention.title: Cancer Prevention & Screening
cancer_prevention.patient_niche: cancer risk screening, oncology prevention counseling

questions.question: What percentage of cancer cases are estimated to be preventable?
questions.explanation: WHO estimates 30-50% of cancer deaths could be prevented by modifying or avoiding key risk factors.

questions.question: What is the single greatest avoidable risk factor for cancer mortality?
questions.explanation: Tobacco use is the single greatest avoidable risk factor for cancer, killing over 8 million people each year.

questions.question: Which vaccines can help reduce the risk of liver and cervical cancer respectively?
questions.explanation: Hepatitis B vaccination reduces liver cancer risk; HPV vaccination reduces cervical cancer risk.

questions.question: Which types of cancer are linked to overweight and obesity?
options: Oesophagus, colorectal, breast, and kidney cancers
questions.correct_answer: Oesophagus, colorectal, breast, and kidney cancers
questions.explanation: Overweight and obesity are linked to multiple cancer types including oesophagus, colorectal, breast, endometrial, and kidney cancers.

questions.question: What can regular cancer screening help achieve?
options: Identify abnormalities early for prompt treatment
Replace the need for a healthy lifestyle
questions.correct_answer: Identify abnormalities early for prompt treatment
questions.explanation: Screening aims to identify pre-cancer or early cancer signs before symptoms develop, enabling prompt treatment.

questions.question: Which practice helps reduce cancer risk related to sun exposure?
questions.explanation: Avoiding excess UV radiation exposure and using sun protection reduces skin cancer risk.

vaccination_immunization.title: Vaccination & Immunization
vaccination_immunization.patient_niche: pediatric patients, immunization counseling, travel health

questions.question: How many lives has global immunization saved over the past 50 years, according to a major study?
questions.explanation: A landmark study found immunization saved an estimated 154 million lives over 50 years, equal to 6 lives every minute.

questions.question: Which vaccine had the most significant impact on reducing infant mortality among those studied?
questions.explanation: The measles vaccine accounted for 60% of the lives saved due to immunization over the past 50 years.

questions.question: How many deaths does immunization currently prevent every year worldwide?
questions.explanation: Immunization currently prevents 3.5 to 5 million deaths annually from diseases like diphtheria, tetanus, and measles.

questions.question: Vaccines are currently available to prevent how many life-threatening diseases and infections?
questions.explanation: We now have vaccines to prevent more than 30 life-threatening diseases and infections.

questions.question: What is a 'zero-dose child' in immunization terminology?
options: A child who has missed all vaccinations
A child who received extra doses
A term with no specific meaning
questions.correct_answer: A child who has missed all vaccinations
questions.explanation: Zero-dose children are those missing out on any vaccination; 13.5 million such children existed globally in 2025.

antimicrobial_resistance_medication_safe.title: Antibiotic & Medication Safety
antimicrobial_resistance_medication_safe.patient_niche: medication adherence programs, antibiotic prescription patients

questions.question: What is antimicrobial resistance (AMR)?
options: When medicines become more effective over time
When bacteria, viruses, fungi, or parasites no longer respond to medicines
questions.correct_answer: When bacteria, viruses, fungi, or parasites no longer respond to medicines
questions.explanation: AMR occurs when microorganisms change over time and no longer respond to antimicrobial medicines.

questions.question: What is one of the main drivers of antimicrobial resistance?
questions.explanation: Misuse and overuse of antimicrobials are the main drivers behind the development of drug-resistant pathogens.

questions.question: Should antibiotics be used to treat viral infections like the common cold?
options: No, unless a bacterial infection is also present
questions.correct_answer: No, unless a bacterial infection is also present
questions.explanation: Antibiotics should not be used for viral infections such as colds and flu unless a bacterial infection is also present.

questions.question: Approximately what fraction of laboratory-confirmed bacterial infections worldwide were resistant to antibiotics in 2023?
questions.explanation: Approximately 1 in 6 laboratory-confirmed bacterial infections worldwide were resistant to antibiotics in 2023.

questions.question: What is one recommended way to help control the spread of antimicrobial resistance?
options: Following routine vaccination and evidence-based prescribing guidelines
Stopping antibiotics early once symptoms improve slightly
questions.correct_answer: Following routine vaccination and evidence-based prescribing guidelines
questions.explanation: Strong infection prevention including vaccination and responsible antibiotic prescribing helps control AMR spread.

stroke_awareness.title: Stroke Awareness & Prevention
stroke_awareness.patient_niche: stroke risk, post-stroke rehabilitation, hypertension patients

questions.question: What was stroke's global ranking as a cause of death and disability in 2021?
questions.explanation: In 2021, stroke was the third leading cause of death and disability globally, with 93.8 million cases.

questions.question: What fraction of adults are predicted to experience a stroke in their lifetime?
questions.explanation: The lifetime risk of stroke has increased by 50% over 20 years, with 1 in 4 adults predicted to experience one.

questions.question: Which of these is a classic warning sign of stroke remembered by the acronym FAST?
options: Face drooping, Arm weakness, Speech difficulty, Time to call emergency services
questions.correct_answer: Face drooping, Arm weakness, Speech difficulty, Time to call emergency services
questions.explanation: Facial droop, arm weakness, and slurred speech are key stroke signs; acting fast by calling emergency services is critical.

questions.question: Which modifiable risk factor contributes most to the global stroke burden?
questions.explanation: High blood pressure is among the top modifiable risk factors driving global stroke burden, along with smoking and poor diet.

questions.question: How much physical activity per week is recommended to help reduce stroke risk?
options: At least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity exercise
questions.correct_answer: At least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity exercise
questions.explanation: WHO recommends at least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity physical activity weekly to help reduce stroke risk.

questions.question: How many servings of fruits and vegetables daily are recommended to help reduce stroke risk?
questions.explanation: WHO recommends at least five servings of fruit and vegetables daily as part of stroke risk reduction.

anemia_blood_health.title: Anemia & Blood Health
anemia_blood_health.patient_niche: anemia, iron deficiency, pregnant women, menstrual health

questions.question: What is the most common nutritional deficiency leading to anaemia?
questions.explanation: Iron deficiency, primarily due to inadequate dietary iron intake, is the most common nutritional cause of anaemia.

questions.question: Which of these is a common symptom of anaemia?
questions.explanation: Common anaemia symptoms include tiredness, dizziness, cold hands and feet, and shortness of breath on exertion.

questions.question: Which nutrient helps the body absorb iron better when eaten together with iron-rich foods?
questions.explanation: Foods rich in vitamin C help the body absorb iron better, while tea, coffee, and calcium can inhibit absorption.

questions.question: Which foods are good sources of dietary iron?
options: Lean red meat, fish, legumes, and dark green leafy vegetables
questions.correct_answer: Lean red meat, fish, legumes, and dark green leafy vegetables
questions.explanation: Iron-rich foods include lean meats, fish, poultry, legumes like lentils and beans, and dark leafy greens.

questions.question: Which population groups are most commonly affected by anaemia?
options: No group is more affected than another
questions.explanation: Young children and pregnant women have the highest global prevalence of anaemia.

questions.question: What should you avoid consuming at the same time as iron supplements to ensure proper absorption?
questions.explanation: Calcium, tea, coffee, and cocoa can inhibit iron absorption, so they should be taken at different times than iron supplements.

food_safety.title: Food Safety
food_safety.patient_niche: gastrointestinal patients, food handlers, general wellness, pediatric care
food_safety.source: WHO Food Safety Fact Sheet, WHO Five Keys to Safer Food

questions.question: Approximately how many people worldwide fall ill from contaminated food each year?
questions.explanation: WHO estimates 866 million people, almost 1 in 9 globally, fall ill from contaminated food annually.

questions.question: Which age group experiences the highest risk of illness from unsafe food?
questions.explanation: Children under 5 face almost three times the risk of illness from unsafe food compared to older children and adults.

questions.question: What are WHO's 'Five Keys to Safer Food'?
options: Keep clean, separate raw and cooked, cook thoroughly, keep food at safe temperatures, use safe water and raw materials
Only wash hands once a day
questions.correct_answer: Keep clean, separate raw and cooked, cook thoroughly, keep food at safe temperatures, use safe water and raw materials
questions.explanation: These five principles form WHO's core food safety guidance used in over 130 countries.

questions.question: What are the most common symptoms of foodborne illness?
questions.explanation: WHO identifies stomach pain, vomiting, and diarrhoea as the most common foodborne illness symptoms.

questions.question: To what minimum internal temperature should meat, poultry, and eggs be cooked to prevent foodborne illness?
questions.explanation: Meat, poultry, eggs, and seafood should be cooked to a minimum internal temperature of 70°C to kill harmful pathogens.

questions.question: Why is it important to separate raw and cooked food during preparation?
options: To prevent cross-contamination of harmful bacteria
questions.correct_answer: To prevent cross-contamination of harmful bacteria
questions.explanation: Separating raw and cooked food prevents harmful bacteria from raw items contaminating ready-to-eat food.

sleep_health.title: Sleep Health
sleep_health.patient_niche: insomnia, general wellness, cardiometabolic risk, mental health patients

questions.question: How many hours of sleep are recommended for adults aged 18-60 for optimal health?
questions.explanation: CDC recommends adults aged 18-60 get 7 or more hours of sleep each night for optimal health.

questions.question: What health risks are associated with consistently sleeping less than 7 hours per night?
options: Increased risk of obesity, diabetes, and heart disease
questions.correct_answer: Increased risk of obesity, diabetes, and heart disease
questions.explanation: Insufficient sleep is linked to increased risk of obesity, diabetes, hypertension, heart disease, and stroke.

questions.question: Approximately what percentage of US adults report getting insufficient sleep?
questions.explanation: Roughly 30.5% of adults reported sleeping less than 7 hours on average in recent CDC data.

questions.question: Which of these is one of five key health behaviors identified for preventing chronic disease?
questions.explanation: CDC identifies sufficient sleep, alongside not smoking, physical activity, moderate alcohol use, and healthy weight, as key chronic-disease-prevention behaviors.

maternal_child_nutrition.title: Maternal & Child Nutrition
maternal_child_nutrition.patient_niche: pregnant women, new mothers, pediatric nutrition, prenatal care

questions.question: How long does WHO recommend exclusive breastfeeding for infants?
questions.explanation: WHO recommends exclusive breastfeeding for the first six months of an infant's life.

questions.question: Up to what age does WHO recommend continuing breastfeeding alongside complementary foods?
options: Up to two years or beyond
questions.correct_answer: Up to two years or beyond
questions.explanation: WHO recommends continued breastfeeding up to two years of age or beyond, alongside safe complementary foods introduced at 6 months.

questions.question: How many child deaths under age 5 could increased breastfeeding potentially prevent?
questions.explanation: WHO estimates that increased breastfeeding could prevent 823,000 deaths in children under 5 annually.

questions.question: What health risk does maternal undernutrition during pregnancy create?
options: Poor fetal development and higher risk of complications
questions.correct_answer: Poor fetal development and higher risk of complications
questions.explanation: Maternal undernutrition leads to poor fetal development and increases pregnancy complication risks.

questions.question: Besides reducing infant mortality, what cancer risk does breastfeeding help lower for mothers?
questions.explanation: WHO notes that breastfeeding helps prevent breast and ovarian cancer in mothers.

burns_first_aid_safety.title: Burns, Injury & First Aid Safety
burns_first_aid_safety.patient_niche: injury prevention, home safety, occupational health, pediatric safety

questions.question: Approximately how many deaths occur globally each year from burns?
questions.explanation: WHO estimates 180,000 deaths occur annually worldwide due to burns, mostly in low- and middle-income countries.

questions.question: What is the correct first-aid step for a fresh thermal burn?
options: Use cool running water to reduce burn temperature
questions.correct_answer: Use cool running water to reduce burn temperature
questions.explanation: WHO recommends cool running water to reduce burn temperature; ice can worsen tissue damage.

questions.question: Which of these should NOT be applied to a burn wound?
questions.explanation: WHO explicitly advises against applying paste, oil, turmeric, or raw cotton to burns as these can worsen injury or cause infection.

questions.question: Where do most burn injuries occur according to WHO data?
questions.explanation: WHO reports that burns occur mainly in the home and workplace, making household safety measures important.

questions.question: What simple home safety measure helps prevent scald burns?
options: Lowering the temperature in hot water taps
There is no way to prevent scalds
questions.correct_answer: Lowering the temperature in hot water taps
questions.explanation: WHO recommends lowering hot water tap temperatures as an effective burn prevention strategy, especially for children.
